clue.text: Engine might get hot, or worse perhaps, with record breaking?

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: the record is breaking into the rearranged letters, sitting inside them
perhaps signals that the words or worse are to be taken in some other arrangement

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A worried motorist wonders whether a hot engine will get worse after a record-breaking run.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's engine and record-breaking run hide the mechanics: hot is just H, and record is the short-play disc EP, not a feat.
explanation.definitionFit: Engine output is measured in this unit of power, so it is what an engine might be said to get or develop.

clue.text: Old newspaperman beginning to succeed in vital area

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter of succeed is placed inside the vital organ

parts.note: the heart is a vital organ or area of the body

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter of the word succeed

explanation.surface: An old press man is starting to make it big in an important region.
explanation.definitionFit: William Randolph Hearst was a famous American newspaper publisher of the early twentieth century.

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the torment word below the Liberal's first letter
leadership of a word is its first letter, here of Liberal

parts.note: torture and anguish both mean extreme suffering

explanation.surface: A political commentator laments that a party has slumped into misery under its Liberal leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline or waste away is to wither in a weakened state, which is this verb's sense.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: paws is a playful word for hands

explanation.surface: A teacher asks pupils to raise their hands if they want a change.
explanation.definitionFit: A change or exchange of one thing for another is a trade, the noun sense here.

clue.text: About right to fill in "hard to swallow"-as the answer!

definitions.text: About right to fill in "hard to swallow"-as the answer!

indicators.note: to fill means the two short pieces go inside the longer word, filling it

parts.note: food that is hard to swallow is literally not fit to eat
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that the phrase hard to swallow can stand in for the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, hard to swallow is food you cannot eat (INEDIBLE); read figuratively it means unbelievable, which is the answer itself, hence the closing remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to swallow is unbelievable, beyond credence, the figurative sense of the whole clue.

clue.text: Priest about to gain badge of rank

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of Priest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman is on the verge of earning a military insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron or band sewn on a uniform sleeve shows military rank, so it is a badge of rank.

clue.text: Mudd's post filled with it, which is rude

parts.note: the setter Mudd refers to himself, so Mudd's is I'm, short for I am

indicators.note: filled with means the post word has the next word placed inside it

parts.note: a pole is an upright post
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter remarks that his post has been stuffed with something offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their own pseudonym for I or ME; here Mudd's is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discourteous or ill-mannered is a near synonym of being rude.

definitions.meaning: to rock is to move gently from side to side
to have influence or control over people, as in holding power

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to rock to and fro and to influence someone's views.

clue.text: Song where backward woman declines an OTT new name? No!

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the whole string of pieces from the end
declines means refuses, so the woman turns down the word an and loses it

parts.note: taken as written, short for over the top
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A songwriter rejects a showy new title, and a shy woman says no to it too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declines' drops AN from WOMAN to leave WOM; 'backward' then turns WOM OTT NEW NAME NO end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional English counting song about a man going out to cut a meadow, a nursery favourite.

parts.note: prog is short for programme, a TV show

explanation.surface: A youngster watches a second television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child or baby.

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
simony is the buying or selling of church offices, a sin in Christian teaching

explanation.surface: A preacher lists greed among the ordinary failings of a Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme reluctance to spend money is miserliness, the meaning of stinginess.

parts.note: one sense is terrified; the other, read literally, is turned into stone, as by a fossilising process

explanation.surface: Someone fears being pelted with rocks, or perhaps of getting high.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means terrified and also, literally, turned to stone.

clue.text: There's no sense in it, for one, yet I climb rocks

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters of yet I climb are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber admits it is pointless, yet scales the rocks anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' rearranges YET I CLIMB into MBECILITY, after I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupidity or foolishness is the state of having no sense in it.

indicators.note: making a comeback means the trimmed word is turned round and read backwards
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: john is American slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A writer called John is nearly ready for a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final T to give TOILE, and 'making comeback' turns that into the writer's surname. John looks like a first name but is the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T S Eliot are both celebrated authors bearing this surname.

clue.text: Boy beginning to blub — crying? Might these comfort him?

parts.note: Teddy is a boy's name, a pet form of Edward

indicators.note: to here means changing over to, so the first letter of the crying word is swapped for the new one

parts.note: crying means shedding tears

indicators.note: beginning of blub picks out its opening letter

explanation.surface: A little boy starts to sob and asks what might console him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' gives B from blub, and 'to' swaps it in for the first letter of TEARS, giving BEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft toy bears are classic comfort objects that soothe a crying child.

parts.note: a celebratory drinking session held to toast a newborn child

explanation.surface: A round of drinks is ordered because a new arrival has come.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom means to have a celebratory drink after a child's birth.

clue.text: Green crown of tooth in decay

indicators.note: crown of a word means its top, here its first letter

parts.note: rusting is decaying through corrosion

explanation.surface: A dentist reports the top of a tooth is rotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naive or gullible, green, means readily believing others.

clue.text: Skidded round crack on a motorway exit

indicators.note: round means the skidded word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: slid means skidded

indicators.note: on places the expert piece directly before the letter a, in an across sense of following on

parts.note: a crack player is an expert, a pro

explanation.surface: A car skidded on a cracked road surface while leaving the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A short road leading off or onto a motorway is an exit or access ramp.

definitions.meaning: general here means approximate, as in a general idea

explanation.definitionFit: The word means stubbly and coarse, and also approximate, as in a ballpark estimate.

indicators.note: opens means the male letter goes into the middle of the flies word

parts.note: hares means rushes or flies along

explanation.surface: A man opens his trouser zip, or a male insect lands among flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim household, the same thing.

definitions.meaning: the spark or mutual attraction between two people
a school science subject taught in the lab or classroom

explanation.definitionFit: The word means romantic attraction and also a science studied at school.

clue.text: Instructed to be stiff, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the stiff word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: taut means tight or stiff

explanation.surface: Someone was trained to stay rigid, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Taught is the past tense of teach, so it means instructed.

clue.text: Conclusion to blazing row left a weird trace of emotion

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters are jumbled
conclusion to a word is its final letter, here of blazing

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a fiery argument, an odd lingering feeling remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges G (end of blazing) with ROW, LEFT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A lingering warm feeling after a happy event is a remnant or trace of emotion.

definitions.meaning: as a prefix it means chief or principal
a curved structure spanning an opening

explanation.definitionFit: The word means chief, as in arch-enemy, and a curved span in a building.

parts.note: to wag is to shake, as a dog's tail
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Shaking a banknote demands payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular payment for work is a pay packet or earnings.

clue.text: The way rake collects last of dirt

indicators.note: collects means the rake word takes in the letter inside it

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a debauched man

indicators.note: last of a word is its final letter, here of dirt

explanation.surface: A garden rake gathers up the last bits of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or path from one place to another.

indicators.note: editing reworks material, so the letters of team reproaching are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film editing crew is criticising the camera operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinematographer is the chief camera operator or director of photography on a film.
